attribution.note: Marcus directly asserts convergence and identifies the five policy needs in his own commentary.

semantics.note: The normalisation preserves the retrospective claim of near-universal agreement, including the named briefers.

contract.note: The contract fairly treats convergence as substantive agreement on the listed needs, allowing equivalent wording and exceptions. It appropriately distinguishes silence from disagreement and accountability from legal liability.

evidence.note: The dated automatic transcript provisionally supports Bengio's agreement on the five themes, including liability insurance. It cannot establish agreement among nearly all speakers.
Altman's recorded proposals support cooperation, safety standards and scrutiny. They do not establish assent to legal liability or the full claim of convergence.
The secondary transcription supports Amodei's endorsement of urgent cooperation, evaluation and verification. It does not establish his agreement on liability or near-universal convergence.

reviews.rationale: The packet supports agreement on several themes but does not establish nearly all speakers' positions across all five needs, especially legal liability. Silence does not demonstrate disagreement, and no substantial affirmative disagreement is established. The incomplete coverage and unverified consequential wording leave both resolution conditions unmet.
